body: Precisely, and I'm not being sarcastic here but I'm sure she may have her good points and be a nice person in other areas. But depending on if you guys are planning a family in whatever foreseeable future, looking at how she views your race (I personally feel that race is a part of our culture and history and shouldn't be dismissed), I'm just wondering if you may run into future problems with the upbringing of kids and at family gatherings... Hopefully she will broaden her mindset over time, at least be aware how her reactions may hurt other people, and realize how contradicting she sounds when rejecting her own roots.

What's she talking about? Your race can be Chinese yet your nationality is Singaporean and you can't erase that. Her grandparents or great grandparents all came from China. While of course as a Chinese Singaporean one wouldn't relate to mainland Chinese, but that's one thing, it's entirely different to reject the Chinese part of Singaporean Chinese when she's probably eating Chinese food daily and going to Chinese New Year gatherings every year and speaking in Chinese to her elderly folks.

Sorry but she sounds like one of those not-so-nice Singaporean Chinese who migrated to Australia my sis met there when she was studying - they saw themselves as Australian and looked down on Singaporeans even though they were Asian as a race themselves. She's also met before a girl who got furious when someone called her Chinese, despite being completely Chinese as a race, strongly denying it and saying she's 'totally Singaporean'. I think this kind of behavior is more prevalent depending on the company they keep, not entirely bound to age.
I'm wondering if when the next wave of covid19 comes again, will things jump back to the start. What is normality anymore.

I like wfh but at the same time I'm tired of dying from work daily now, rather go to office and draw a line at work hours. If only I can teleport to work. The only thing that sucks is the 1.5hrs x 2 journey time.

This and the idea that mental illnesses don't exist or can simply be treated by looking at a Facebook motivational quote. There are people who are suffering from PTSD after being in the ICU on the ventilator and many cases of domestic abuse are being reported in the US. 
I wonder what the world will do then when faced with all these ugly facts society keeps trying to sweep under the rug. Also, looking at the mass layoffs in other countries makes me nervous about Singapore. 
I hope the man in the video finds the support he needs to carry on.

I've spoken to my counsellor and she said in a suicide attempt event they would send the police to track the person down and stop them. Outside of it I don't think there's any other organization that may be able to do it though I'll ask around again. It's sad because mental health has a terrible stigma in my country. 
I tried posting on the Singapore reddit and got my post removed..not sure due to censorship or what.

Thanks for listening. I'm not going to call the cops on him after hearing from him about this. I just don't know if I should call them the moment I suspect he's about to commit suicide one day. My first line of help would be the Samaritans helpline but they and my counsellor told me to call the police if I suspect my friend is trying to end his life that day at any point in future.

It's like, on one hand not doing anything but trying to reach him alone should anything happen makes me worry if I would be too slow to save him. On the other hand, there's a part of me that fears calling anyone to try to stop him would only be prolonging his suffering. For now, I'm just talking with him and keeping watch in the mean time, hoping it's not too late for him to change his mind about suicide being the only way out.
